articles.title: Gretchen Whitmer may punt on education tax credit, won’t run for president
articles.description: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer says she won’t run for president and may not decide by the Jan. 1 deadline whether to opt Michigan into a Trump administration school tax credit program.
articles.content: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer is hesitant to opt in to the Trump administration’s federal school tax credit starting next year Whitmer told Detroit-area leaders at a Friday event that it may make more sense for Gov.-elect Jocelyn Benson to decide Whitmer also said she won’t run for president and reflected on her relationship with Trump and her legacy as governor BIRMINGHAM — Outgoing Gov. Gretchen Whitmer isn’t yet sold on signing Michigan up for the Trump administration’s federal school tax credit program, telling a group of Detroit-area business and community leaders Friday that the decision might be better left to her successor. Whitmer said she hasn’t made a final call on opting into the Education Freedom Tax Credit, designed to offer taxpayers federal income tax credits of up to $1,700 in exchange for donating to scholarship granting organizations. Those groups would then distribute the money to eligible students for education expenses, including private school tuition. States have to let the Trump administration know by Jan. 1 whether they’re opting in. That will be Gov.-elect Jocelyn Benson’s first day in office. Related What to know about school tax credit program. Will Michigan opt in? Jocelyn Benson has big plans. Michigan has big problems Michigan Democrats promised lower costs. Here are 7 ideas More than 30 states have already signed up, including some with Democratic governors, but Whitmer said Friday that even if she were to do so, “there’s no guarantee that the next administration will actually implement it and see it through.” “So opting in, at this juncture, I don’t know makes a whole lot of sense for us,” she said at a Detroit Free Press Breakfast Club event, noting that the incoming Benson administration “will have time to do it on Jan. 1 if they want to.” Speaking with reporters after the event, Whitmer said she sees upsides and downsides to the tax credit program. “But I don’t know that it’s appropriate for me to obligate the next administration,” she said, noting that she’s discussed the matter with Benson. “Everyone’s grappling with the arguments on both sides to figure out what makes the most sense for Michigan.” Benson, a fellow Democrat, criticized the tax credit program in September, saying that it would be “reckless and irresponsible” to “commit taxpayer dollars to a program under Trump’s control with zero transparency or assurance it will deliver for Michigan students.” Some business and education leaders want Whitmer to opt in while she has the chance, arguing the program, created under the Trump administration’s “One Big Beautiful Bill,” helps raise money for students to succeed in schools of their choice, whether public or private.Donate But critics view the program as a backdoor, voucher-like way to divert public dollars to private schools, which is generally prohibited under the state Constitution. Forty-nine Democratic legislators this week signed a letter urging Whitmer not to opt in. Whitmer could not seek reelection due to the state’s term-limits law and will leave office at noon on Jan. 1. Benson will be sworn in then and will begin her term with a Democratic majority in both chambers of the Legislature. In Friday’s wide-ranging discussion with Detroit Free Press columnist and television journalist Carol Cain, Whitmer also reflected on her legacy as governor, offered advice for incoming elected officials, shared more details about her up-and-down relationship with President Donald Trump — and once again insisted that she won’t run for president in 2028. Talks with Trump During her first term, Whitmer and Trump frequently clashed on COVID-19 policy, and the president’s frequent attacks on her leadership drew national attention to her actions as governor. Trump’s insults from that time were a “low point” in her tenure as governor, Whitmer said Friday, “not because it hurt my feelings or because I couldn’t take criticism.” “It was a low point because I was worried that they would withhold support,” she continued. “We needed masks. We needed gloves … and that was my fear, that they would be petty and withhold things.” That relationship evolved after Trump won reelection in 2024, when Whitmer developed a working relationship with the president even as she disagreed with him on issues like steep Canadian tariffs. Whitmer said Friday that Trump “still calls me every once in a while,” recalling one notable post-primary discussion where he asked her whether Republican US Senate candidate Mike Rogers had a shot at winning Michigan. “I said, ‘Not with your tariffs,’” Whitmer told the crowd, adding that she hoped in vain that her candor would convince Trump to shift strategy. “I wasn’t trying to help Mike Rogers, by the way.” What’s next? Not a run for president, Whitmer said, noting a “big group of people” are likely to “duke it out” in 2028, but “it ain’t going to be me.” “How many times do I have to answer this question?” the governor added. Whitmer said she hasn’t decided what her next steps are after she leaves office, though she said she has “a lot of energy, and I want to make sure that I’m doing things that make me feel good, but also keep me challenged and excited.” “I am going to try to be still for a little while and think about how I want to spend my next season,” she said. Asked whether she had any words of wisdom for Benson, US Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed or other incoming Democratic officials, she said her only advice was “you’ve got to deliver.” “It’s one thing to win the election, and another thing to do the work,” she said. Benson is “ready” for the job and doesn’t need her advice, Whitmer said, but should she ask for it, “I will be a phone call away.”

articles.content: When the Steam Machine first started shipping in June, Valve said it was producing fewer units at a higher price than initially planned because it couldn't secure supplies of scarce RAM and storage components at a reasonable cost. Now, as the last of the initial batch of Steam Machine reservations are finally being fulfilled, Valve says those supply and cost issues will continue into the foreseeable future and may even require a price change. "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels," Valve wrote in a blog post on Thursday. "As a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained." articles.title: Michigan advocates launch coalition to push paid leave, universal childcare and higher wages
articles.description: A new coalition of advocacy organizations, pushing for policies that enable a living wage, universal childcare and paid family and medical leave, launched this week as affordability takes center stage in political conversations around Michigan and nationwide. Jayme Vosovic, the community engagement director at the Michigan League for Public Policy, explained that the coalition, called […]
articles.content: Getty ImagesA new coalition of advocacy organizations, pushing for policies that enable a living wage, universal childcare and paid family and medical leave, launched this week as affordability takes center stage in political conversations around Michigan and nationwide. Jayme Vosovic, the community engagement director at the Michigan League for Public Policy, explained that the coalition, called Families Rising, stemmed from a series of listening sessions hosted around the state by the Michigan League for Public Policy and Michigan United in which participants were asked what makes it hard for their families to get by. “No matter where we went, the three main issues that kept coming up were jobs with no paid leave, so getting sick or having a baby means losing a paycheck, childcare that costs as much as rent, if you can even find it at all, and wages that haven’t kept up with the price of groceries or rent,” Vosovic said. “We know these are not separate problems. They hit the same families at the same time, and we know that no single organization can fix them alone. So we knew we had to find strength in numbers.” Leaders from various coalition members spoke about the importance of each of the three policy priorities. Christina Hayes, a community organizer at Mothering Justice, said that, when talking with mothers and caregivers, they often find themselves “sandwiched” between caring for sick or elderly loved ones and raising their own children, all while employed, demonstrating the need for paid family leave policies. McDonald Rivet speaks to Saginaw parents about childcare costs, highlights tax credit bill “Paid leave protects financial security,” she said. “Families should never have to lose their income or risk falling behind on rent, utilities, groceries, while dealing with the family emergency.” Hayes added that paid leave also acknowledges how many Michigan families serve as caregivers. “Many residents are caring for aging parents, children with disabilities, or people that are facing serious illnesses,” she said. Mori Anderson, a mother who said that she lives with kidney failure, explained exactly how important paid leave is for her to be able to survive. “For me, paid leave is about more than time away from work. It’s about having the freedom to take care of myself, show up for my children, and maintain my livelihood without being penalized for circumstances beyond my control,” she said. “Healthcare equity must include workplace policies that allow for people to actually have access to the care that they need. Navigating a job with a disability should not require sacrificing your health.” Wende Randall, the director of the Kent County Essential Needs Task Force, said universal childcare has positive impacts for early childhood development by exposing children to environments and social settings outside of their home, as well as in economic stability for families by reducing the pressures that limit the ability of parents to work. GET THE MORNING HEADLINES. SUBSCRIBE Kermit Williams, the political director of Oakland Forward, added that he hopes to see legislation with a floor of $25 per hour by 2028 — a wage that half of Americans do not make, he said. “We have people that are working two or three jobs and still qualify for government benefits and assistance right now,” he said. “If we were to put a living wage in Michigan, we would be able not only to raise the economy that we need, but we would be able to make sure that people have time to spend with their families, their loved ones, their kids, pay for sick individuals, and other things that they need in order to survive and thrive.” Many of the organizations involved with Families Rising have spoken at length since the midterm elections, in which Michigan Democrats won their trifecta on a largely affordability-focused platform, about the need to enact the policies on which officials campaigned on, focused on lowering costs for Michiganders. Hayes and Randall both noted that the coalition has been in conversations with returning and incoming legislators to find those who are willing to sponsor and champion legislation with these policies, as Democrats prepare to take a trifecta in Michigan’s state government. “We stay ready, so we don’t have to get ready. So even before the elections were going on, we were watching who was even running, and we already have our elected official champions lined up,” Hayes said.

articles.content: A Mount Clemens cannabis retail shop faces the prospect of closing up, leaving 40 people out of work following a third vote by city leaders to revoke the store’s operating certificate. The Mount Clemens City Commission voted 6-1 Monday, Nov. 16 to not renew a permit to 222 BIz, LCC, doing business as Joyology Cannabis Dispensary, on Malow Street off Groesbeck Highway. Commissioner Roxanne Brown cast the sole vote against the revocation, but did not comment on her vote. At issue was the pot shop’s lack of progress on constructing a parking lot, which apparently started two years ago. This fall, the commission voted twice to give Joyology additional time finish work on the parking lot, which still isn’t done. Noting the commission has repeatedly pushed back the deadline for the lot, Commissioner Spencer Calhoun said it’s likely everyday residents would not receive a similar break from the city. “It’s a disrespect to the businesses and residents to let this go on any further,” Calhoun said at Monday’s administrative hearing. According to Mount Clemens officials, the company opened in August 2025, with the knowledge it needed to repair the parking lot. The work was supposed to start in April, but the cannabis shop encountered delays and provided little to no communication with city officials. City Manager Gregg Shipman said Joyology received a temporary certificate of occupancy in order to open the dispensary. He said since the work to be done was in the parking lot, he viewed the building as safe to open to the public. As months passed without any sign of the work’s progress, the city revoked the company’s temporary occupancy permit. In September, commissioners agreed to revoke the permit, unless “significant and meaningful” progress was made. One month later, the cannabis shop said progress was being made but asked for another extension, which the city granted, but commissioners asked for updates on the progress. At Monday’s administrative hearing, Chris Yermian, owner and director of operations at the cannabis shop, asked for another extension, saying construction was nearly finished. He blamed the delays on the construction company, noting that there currently is a large demand for construction contractors. “I take this very seriously,” he told the commission. “The contractor keeps telling me ‘we are just days away’ from finishing the job.” Shutting them down would destroy their $1 million-plus investment as well as end jobs for about 40 employees, according to company officials. On Tuesday evening, a reporter visiting the site saw the parking lot has been paved, but still had not been striped. Piles of dirt and construction equipment were left near the front entrance. City Attorney Rob Huth said the commission must forward its findings to the state Cannabis Regulatory Agency (CRA), which oversees licensing, compliance, and enforcement for adult-use marijuana. He said the CRA will be told Joyology failed to comply with a local site plan and engineering approvals., and has become a “public nuisance.” Once the CRA is notified of Mount Clemens’ decision, Joyology must stop its retail sales as the store cannot legally sell cannabis without local authorization in place. Depending on what the CRA decides, a license may be closed, surrendered, placed on hold/suspension, or moved into a “closed pending” status as it prepares to close. Joyology has shops in Lake Orion, Monroe, and New Buffalo. Its store in Center Line is listed as “temporarily closed” on their website.

Warren police seek to prevent scams involving cryptocurrency
articles.content: Warren police have launched an effort to counter an increase in scammers who use cryptocurrency kiosks and Bitcoin ATMs to help them steal large sums of money from victims. Warning signs are being placed next to the several cryptocurrency ATM locations in Warren, done partly in recognition of International Fraud Awareness Week that started Nov. 15. The program is in response to a rise in cryptocurrency-related fraud cases in Warren, with 73 victims losing a total of $2.8 million in 2025 and through mid-October this year, police said in a press release. That is an average of $38,666 per case. Victims have ranged in age from 18 to 87, police said. “This campaign came directly from one of our frontline officers, and it was a practical solution that just made complete sense,” said Warren Police Commissioner Eric Hawkins. “Our goal is to have these warning signs beside every crypto ATM in the city, ensuring our residents keep their hard-earned money, rather than handing it over to ruthless scammers.” Unfortunately, no arrests have been made in Warren, according to police Lt. John Gajewski. “Many of the investigations lead to persons/organizations outside of the U.S. which makes further investigation, let alone criminal prosecution, very difficult,” Gajewski. “So sadly, we do not have any arrests stemming from these cases. That is why our goal is to educate potential victims and hope they keep their money before turning it over.” Scams involving virtual currency also have been rising in Michigan and nationally. In 2025, Michigan residents lost $210 million in cryptocurrency scams, an increase from $126 million in 2025 and $80 million in 2023, according to FBI statistics. The number of complaints rose to 3,648 last year after there were about 3,000 in 2024. Nationally, there were 181,565 fraud complaints involving crypto resulted in $11.4 billion in losses in 2025, the FBI said. The cities of Sterling Heights, Harper Woods and Grosse Pointe Farms have passed ordinances regulating or banning the machines. Sterling Height’s ordinance passed last January created licensing and operating regulations for the machines. It sets a daily transaction limit of $2,000 ($1,000 for new users) and a monthly transaction limit of $10,000. “This ordinance gives us the tools to better regulate this industry and deter predatory activity,” said Sterling Heights Mayor Michael Taylor. Sterling Heights officials said last December that police investigated 23 fraud cases involving losses of more than $542,000, with seniors representing most victims. There are also pending bills in the state House of Representatives and Senate to address cryptocurrency kiosks and Bitcoin ATMs. State Attorney General Dana Nessell reissued a warning about such scams last April. “If you receive a call from someone claiming to be from an agency or company who demands you use a Bitcoin ATM to pay a fine or bill, it is most certainly a scam,” Nessel said. “Before taking any action, hang up, breathe, and verify any claims.” Nessel said a legitimate company or government agency will never ask somone to deposit money into a cryptocurrency kiosk such as a Bitcoin ATM, and to beware of urgent requests. Warren officers said most scam victims “are initially targeted via phone calls, social media, emails, device pop-up alerts, or text messages.” “Scammers frequently impersonate legitimate entities such as government agencies, police departments, the IRS, banks, and businesses, to coerce unsuspecting individuals into withdrawing cash and depositing it into cryptocurrency ATMs,” police said. “Victims often believe they are resolving urgent account issues, settling fake jury duty fines, paying off false claims involving child pornography, or taking advantage of investment and rental opportunities.” Experts say that once the cash is converted into crypto, it is nearly impossible to reverse the transaction. Warren police have created laminated “Scam Alert” signs to be placed adjacent to an estimated 15 to 30 cryptocurrency kiosks in local businesses, subject to approval from the businesses, police said. “These high-visibility warnings are designed to give potential victims a crucial moment to pause, independently verify the situation, and request police assistance before completing a Transaction,” police said..”Alongside the public outreach, Warren officers are receiving specialized training on cryptocurrency scam red flags, and all reported incidents will continue to be forwarded to the department’s dedicated fraud investigator for full investigation.”

articles.content: Tech companies are racing to figure out how AI can make everyday work a little easier. From notetakers to webcams that follow your movements, here are six AI-powered gadgets worth checking out if you want to upgrade your workspace. If you’re constantly scribbling notes during meetings, the Flowtica Scribe could save you from having to type everything up afterward. The AI-powered pen combines traditional handwriting with audio recording. You can use its built-in gel pen to take notes, tap the side to highlight important points, and press the end of the pen to start recording audio. Once the meeting is over, its AI can transcribe the conversation, summarize key takeaways, and create a to-do list based on what was discussed. You can even ask the AI questions about the meeting to find specific information without having to go through the entire recording. The Scribe comes with a built-in microphone and 32GB of onboard storage. It can also identify up to 15 different speakers and supports 92 languages. Anker’s AI-powered recording pin, Soundcore Work, is designed to capture conversations, meetings, and quick voice memos without taking up much space on your desk. Priced at $159 (currently reduced to $99 in the Amazon Black Friday sale), the coin-sized device comes with a puck-shaped charging case and can record for up to eight hours on a single charge, extending to 32 hours when used with its case. Anker also claims a recording range of up to 5 meters, making it useful for capturing conversations around a meeting table. The companion app handles transcription and uses AI to turn recordings into more organized notes and summaries. Users also get 300 minutes of free audio transcription each month. If you need more recording capacity or access to additional AI features, Anker offers optional subscription plans, including Pro ($99 per year) and Unlimited ($239 per year). Logitech’s MX Keypad brings AI shortcuts directly to your desk, with dedicated buttons that let you launch your preferred AI assistant or trigger specific productivity tools with a single press. If you frequently switch between different apps and AI assistants, having these shortcuts within reach could make your workday easier. The keypad can be configured to work with tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, along with a range of popular productivity and creative apps, such as OpenAI Codex, Microsoft Teams, PowerPoint, Excel, Notion, Slack, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Zoom, and Figma. Amazon’s Kindle Scribe Colorsoft brings color to the company’s digital notetaking lineup and offers some neat AI features designed to clean up your messy notes. Starting at $479, the device is aimed at people who regularly work with digital documents, including students, researchers, and professionals who prefer annotating files rather than printing them out. It lets you highlight important passages, mark up documents, organize handwritten notes, and sketch out ideas. Notably, the Scribe Colorsoft incorporates AI-powered tools to clean up messy handwriting, straighten highlighting and underlining, summarize notes, and help turn scattered thoughts into more organized information. Its search feature can look across your saved notes to find specific details and help identify connections between different entries. If you’re tired of adjusting your webcam during video calls, Insta360’s Link 2 Pro aims to take care of that for you. Priced at $249 (discounted to $199 for Black Friday), this AI-powered webcam combines 4K video capture with intelligent tracking and automatic framing. Its smart video tracker can follow your movements and adjust the camera’s position to keep you in view, even when you move around your workspace, which is particularly useful for people who regularly give presentations, teach online, or switch between sitting at their desk and standing during video calls. The camera also offers group tracking, which can come in handy during team meetings or presentations involving multiple people. AI-powered noise cancellation is another useful addition, helping reduce distracting background sounds during calls. Your desk could probably use a little intelligence, too. Autonomous Desk Pro is an adjustable standing desk designed to encourage healthier habits throughout the workday. Beyond switching between sitting and standing positions, the AI-powered desk uses built-in sensors to monitor your activity and remind you when it’s time to move, stretch, or change positions. It can track how much time you spend sitting versus standing, giving you a better idea of your daily work habits. The AI features go a step further by allowing you to ask questions about your activity. For example, you can check how long you’ve been sitting, compare your activity with the previous day, or get information about the room’s CO2 levels to help determine whether it’s time to open a window. articles.title: Detroit launches $12M initiative to address homelessness
articles.description: Detroit is one of eight communities selected for the funding. The money — $3 million each year through September 2030 — is expected to help more than 2,100 Detroiters.
articles.content: Detroit will use $12 million to bring together a broad swath of services — from psychiatric resources to housing supports — to help people facing homelessness who have substance use disorders and mental health issues. City officials and partners announced details for how Detroit plans to use the federal four-year grant on Thursday, Nov. 19. It’s part of the Trump administration’s Safety Through Recovery, Engagement and Evidence-based Treatment and Support (STREETS) program. Detroit is one of eight communities selected for the funding. The money — $3 million each year through September 2030 — is expected to help more than 2,100 Detroiters. “We know that homelessness rarely occurs in isolation. Research shows that people experiencing homelessness are disproportionately impacted by serious mental illness and then also for those who use substances (there’s) increased risk of fatal overdose,” said Valencia Lyle, the city of Detroit’s director of behavioral health initiatives at the CHASS Center in southwest Detroit. “This grant gives us the opportunity to change that trajectory through connecting people to treatment, recovery supports, stability and ultimately housing.” Valencia Lyle, the city of Detroit’s director of behavioral health initiatives at the CHASS Center in southwest Detroit. Credit: City of Detroit Flickr Homelessness can have multiple root causes, from mental health challenges and substance use to evictions and affordability hurdles. One limited snapshot of homelessness on a single night in January this year showed that homelessness is increasing in the Detroit area. How will the program support Detroiters? The program, dubbed Detroit PATHS, is expected to enroll 75 residents into treatment for mental health and substance use, help house 25 people and train 500 frontline workers on how to respond to individuals who have behavioral health needs. The city’s Human, Homeless, and Family Services and Health departments will lead the efforts. Detroit PATHS will support Detroit’s current homeless outreach and behavioral health efforts, expand weekly psychiatric services directly to residents through street medicine, offer specialized training for public safety personnel and shelter staff and help people into housing. The program is a partnership between the city of Detroit, Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network (DWIHN), Wayne County and homeless service providers, health care agencies and community groups. Lyle said the goal is to bring partners together. “Our city of Detroit homeless outreach team will work hand in hand with the Homeless Action Network of Detroit to make those initial connections,” she said. “From there, CHASS’ street medicine team will bring medical and psychiatric care directly to people where they are. We’re also focused on young people, including those aging out of foster care.” Luke Shaefer, Detroit’s top health, human services and poverty solutions leader. Credit: City of Detroit Flickr During an October visit touting the program, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. referred to people without homes and with mental health issues and substance use disorders in the city as “the most destitute and lonely, isolated, decrepit community.” He suggested the new program would give them “the opportunity for redemption and recovery.” Luke Shaefer, Detroit’s top health, human services and poverty solutions leader, distanced the city from the health secretary’s remarks. “We would not align with those comments, and this particular press conference was a statement to say what we believe is the intention of the grant in working in partnership with our federal partners, to come together in a coordinated approach, a dignified approach, which is completely embedded in the mayor’s vision for what we’re doing together,” he said on Thursday. Free Press reporter Kristen Jordan Shamus contributed to this report. Reach reporter Nushrat Rahman at nrahman@freepress.com.

articles.title: University of Michigan regents approve $785 million Los Alamos computing center project
articles.description: The University of Michigan Board of Regents voted Thursday to proceed with work on the computing center — which opponents refer to as a data center — the university is developing with Los Alamos National Laboratory. The project is planned for a site on Textile Road in Ypsilanti Township despite across-the-board opposition from the community’s […]
articles.content: Rendering of the University of Michigan and Los Alamos National Laboratory computing center. (Courtesy of the University of Michigan)The University of Michigan Board of Regents voted Thursday to proceed with work on the computing center — which opponents refer to as a data center — the university is developing with Los Alamos National Laboratory. The project is planned for a site on Textile Road in Ypsilanti Township despite across-the-board opposition from the community’s elected officials. As a state university, Michigan does not require local zoning approval for the project to move forward. The vote was 7-1, with Regent Paul Brown voting no. Regent Carl Myers said he’s excited about the scientific work that will be conducted at the facility, which he said will include cancer, clean energy, and extreme weather research. “We worked very hard to find the right balance between the project and the community, and I think we’ve been successful,” he said. The university says it will commit $5 million to projects in the greater Ypsilanti area over the next five years. The Michigan and Los Alamos project has attracted significant community pushback. Residents and local leaders say the Ann Arbor university is targeting a neighboring community with more low-income areas and communities of color for a project that will add costs for Ypsilanti Township residents without providing substantial benefits. Community members have also raised concerns about noise, generator emissions, and other environmental impacts from the 100 megawatt project. The Textile Road site is located on the Huron River. “We will not have any negative impact on the Huron River,” outgoing Michigan President Domenico Grasso said in a Thursday statement. Phase one of the project includes the development of 150,000 gross square feet. Phases one and two are not expected to exceed 300,000 gross square feet, according to the memo Robert Hewlett, university chief financial officer and executive vice president, submitted to the regents seeking project approval. The project’s first phase will cost an estimated $450 million, with the cost of phase one and two not to exceed $785 million, Hewlett said. A State of Michigan grant and university bond proceeds with debt service from a combination of rental payments and general fund resources will fund the project’s first phase, according to Hewlett. Thursday’s vote authorizes the issuing of bids and awarding of contracts for the project. The project received a $100 million grant in 2024 from the Michigan Strategic Fund and Michigan Economic Development Corp., a taxpayer-funded agency providing business incentives. A community partnership and investment resolution attached to Hewlett’s request for action says the university should build on successful programs in the Ypsilanti area like those at the University of Michigan Health Ypsilanti Health Center. The facility provides care for residents who might otherwise need to travel to Ann Arbor, and brings patients and workers to downtown Ypsilanti, according to the document. Michigan said it will develop and enact a comprehensive community partnership program for Ypsilanti Township focused on education, parks and recreation, partnerships with community organizations, and identifying and funding public safety initiatives, environmental enhancements and other projects to improve residents’ quality of life. articles.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
articles.description: Signal users on iOS will see this option to toggle blocking screenshots and preventing Siri AI from scanning on-screen content. | Image: Signal Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users' messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the
articles.content: Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users’ messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy,” Signal president Meredith Whittaker said in a blog post, while urging OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access. “We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” Whittaker said. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.” Signal is addressing the privacy concerns by blocking the ability to take screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and Android, which should prevent Siri, Gemini, and other Android AI assistants from reading on-screen content. Users can restore screenshot capabilities in Signal’s app settings, but Whittaker warns that doing so will “potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees.” Whittaker admits that Signal’s screenshot-blocking remedy is “incomplete,” as it doesn’t address alternative ways that AI agents can access app data, such as retrieving it via the device file system. [Image: Signal’s app security settings on Android devices will display this message for the screenshot-blocking feature. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/protecting-your-privacy-2.png?quality=90&strip=all] Signal took a similar approach last year to prevent Microsoft’s controversial Recall feature from capturing secured chats. The encrypted messaging service says it’s struggling to develop a better solution due to the lack of available information regarding how AI agents are actually accessing application data, and is now calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide “simple technical tools and accurate documentation” to app developers. Signal also says more tools are needed to prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from using deep accessibility settings in apps like a “skeleton key” to access application data. “We all need to recognize that the current integration of AI agents into the operating system, without these common-sense remedies, represents an existential threat to privacy at the application layer, and the ability of independent developers like Signal to protect your sensitive data,” said Whittaker. “Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem and should galvanize anyone who cares about these fundamental rights.”

articles.title: How to fix text to speech accuracy problems
articles.description: Text to speech not working? Learn how to fix text to speech accuracy problems like mispronounced words, robotic delivery, and API errors with these tips.
articles.content: Introducing Eleven v4Meet Eleven v4, our most emotive model yet. While they’re trained on massive voice datasets and can consistently produce high-fidelity audio, most text to speech (TTS) models can still mispronounce words or run into other speech issues. Mispronunciations happen when a TTS engine encounters words and phrases outside the range of speech in its training dataset. That happens most often with industry jargon, brand names, or proper names. TTS engines may also generate rushed, stilted, or robotic speech when text passages are long or punctuated for reading rather than structured to be spoken out loud. You may also encounter a few common technical issues connecting your applications to TTS engines via API. In this article, we’ll explore these three categories of issues and common ways to resolve each. Text to speech problems broadly fall into three categories. The TTS model misreads novel words or phrases. e.g., your brand name, industry jargon, acronyms, or homographs. The output speech is monotonous, pauses at odd points, or rushes through passages that need slower delivery. Your application doesn’t generate speech for one or more technical reasons, such as missed voice IDs, workload limits, or broken API keys. This guide breaks down each of these three issues in more detail so you can understand exactly what kind of output quality or technical issue you’re facing. Understanding them will help you identify the right solution faster. Engineers train modern neural voice models on massive speech datasets. They’re able to generate natural-sounding speech in almost countless combinations of words. However, no training dataset is ever universal. There are always going to be edge-case pronunciations and obscure words or proper names the model won’t speak correctly. This won’t happen often, but everyone who uses TTS models regularly should be prepared for how to handle it when it happens. First, it’s important to understand why these mispronunciations occur. Speech synthesis models work by converting text into speech using a process called grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion. Phonemes are the smallest units of spoken sound. Graphemes are the smallest units of written language, typically one letter, that represent a phoneme. When text input doesn’t match the spelling patterns the models encountered in training data, they take their best guess as to the phonetic pronunciation. Sometimes this leads to mispronunciations. Businesses often use creative spellings for brand names. They catch the eye, but often also confound speech synthesis models. Creative first names and surnames can as well, for the same reason. When a model encounters an unfamiliar name, it tries to apply the basic phonetic rules it learned. That output speech might be far off from what you want. Think about the acronym NASA. Imagine you’ve never seen it before, much like a speech model might. Do you pronounce it “N.A.S.A.” or “nasuh?” What about a software API? Is that “A.P.I.” or “apee?” What if your company is selling a brand new software tool with a new acronym? You can guarantee it’s not in a speech model’s training data. So the model would have to guess how you wanted it pronounced unless you gave it custom instructions. Homographs are words that share spellings but have different pronunciations depending on context. For example, the word “read” is spelled the same but pronounced differently in the past and present tenses. A speech model will need sufficient contextual understanding to determine how to pronounce homographs as you wish. Long sentences of technical jargon can pile obscure words on top of specific pronunciations and acronyms in short order. What might be an unnoticeable error by itself can quickly become part of flat, robotic speech as a model tries to parse many unfamiliar words and phrasings. You don’t need to completely rewrite your scripts to avoid these scenarios. Modern neural speech models include two tools to fix them efficiently, case by case: pronunciation dictionaries and phonetic script tags. Dictionaries are best when you have a body of custom pronunciations that recur regularly across your TTS projects. For example, if your company sells medical devices and your scripts regularly contain technical terms, medical procedures, and other domain-specific content. The W3C-standard Pronunciation Lexicon Specification (PLS) format provides a structure for mapping those terms to specific phonetic pronunciations using International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) notation. The International Phonetic Alphabet is a standardized alphabet of all possible speech sounds. The speech model checks your dictionary as it reads the script and refers to your listed pronunciations whenever it encounters words in your dictionary. Phoneme entries work only with the eleven_v4, eleven_v4_turbo, eleven_flash_v2, and eleven_v3 models. On other models, use alias rules instead. PLS files are case sensitive, so add both “tomato” and “Tomato” if you need both. Phonetic tags are usually the better choice when you need to tweak single lines in a script. Rather than generating a dictionary, you use in-line phonetic tags that prompt the speech model to say a word how you want according to the IPA. For example, let’s say you’re writing a podcast script and you want to reference an industry expert two or three times. Instead of adding it to your corporate pronunciation dictionary, you just tag her name with the correct pronunciation when you use it in the script. Dictionaries and tags are useful for managing issues with individual words in speech output, but they don’t address overall delivery, cadence, and speech dynamics. When writing a script, it’s important to frame your text with the understanding that it’s going to be spoken aloud. Your word choices, turns of phrase, and punctuation often should be different from that of text meant simply to be read. Approach your script writing with the mindset of a speech writer: “How do I want this spoken aloud? Where do we pause for dramatic effect? Where do we speed up?” Those questions apply to a script for advanced neural speech models just as much as to a script you’d write for a person. You don’t want to leave any ambiguity in your scripts. Neural speech models understand context well, but they perform best when they don’t have to guess. Abbreviations and shorthand are common items they might stumble over. For example, a script might say, “You’re looking for a figure close to 15m.” Does the writer want the TTS engine to say “fifteen million” or “fifteen meters?” Write it out so the model doesn’t have to guess from context. Punctuation plays an important role in written text, but it matters even more in text to speech synthesis. Punctuation controls the rhythm. It represents different types of pauses you can use to break up complex thoughts or simply to maintain a natural cadence that’s more comfortable for someone to listen to. Models are most likely to stumble over or rush long, conditional, multi-clause sentences. Break those apart into shorter statements of varied length. This gives the model more breathing room and prevents it from rushing when it tries to find the cadence for long, run-on sentences. If you’re synthesizing speech pulled from a content management system or other business system, it might contain HTML, JSON, Markdown, or other formatting. Remove this and format it as text to get the most natural-sounding speech. Speech models may struggle to understand when to ignore those tags, read them literally, or incorporate them contextually into their output. You can explore mispronunciation and other issues more at length in the ElevenLabs troubleshooting guide. Teams that produce voice audio at scale typically connect their applications to a speech synthesis model by API. This makes production more efficient overall, but it adds a technical layer you need to manage on top of the model's speech output. The ElevenLabs API error code reference covers response codes in detail, but here are the four most common HTTP status codes encountered when troubleshooting text to speech integrations, and how to address them. A 400 status code response from a speech model API means your application sent data the model couldn’t process. In TTS workflows, that typically stems from hitting character limits or accidentally sending blank inputs. Every TTS request you send has a character limit set by the model. If you try sending more text than the model’s limit allows, the TTS server will return this error. Limits per request are 10,000 characters for eleven_v4 and eleven_multilingual_v2, 5,000 for eleven_v3, 30,000 for eleven_flash_v2, and 40,000 for eleven_flash_v2_5, on every plan. To resolve this issue, split longer scripts into multiple sections the model can process sequentially. A TTS engine will reject any payloads that contain empty strings (empty_text). Include cleaning steps in your input pipeline to remove empty lines so the server doesn’t reject an otherwise workable payload. A 401 error code means the API gateway rejected your credentials and your payload wasn’t passed to the model. This happens when there’s an issue with the API key. Your request to the model server needs to include a valid xi-api-key. If it doesn’t, the server will return a 401 error. Verify that your key is actually present in the request and hasn’t been revoked, expired, or truncated from headers in deployment. The API returns invalid_api_key when the key is wrong and missing_api_key when none is sent. You receive a 404 error when the endpoint can’t find the TTS resource specified in the URL request. This might occur if you send the wrong voice_id parameter or it’s just missing from the request URL. Make sure you’ve received the correct voice_id to use. Verify it’s actually present in the path parameters and not mistyped. The API returns voice_not_found when the voice ID doesn’t exist. This error has two distinct causes: you’ve hit your concurrent request limit for your service tier or the TTS platform is throttling requests to manage a spike in traffic. Each subscription tier to a TTS engine specifies a fixed number of concurrent requests you can send. If your applications exceed that limit, the server will return this type of 429 error. Build an asynchronous queuing layer using a service such as Redis to meter your outgoing payloads so they don’t exceed your tier limits. Or assess whether a higher tier subscription is cost-effective. Under heavy load, a TTS server may throttle incoming requests to maintain performance. Build automated retry logic into your application’s API client. Make sure it can retry with exponential backoff and then fail gracefully after a maximum number of attempts. A quick web app test is usually insufficient quality control for large-scale TTS payloads. The cost of bad runs can add up quickly. Test your script in a series of controlled iterations before you submit. That upfront preparation will help you produce the highest-quality voice audio most efficiently. Usually your problems will be specific passages or just specific words or names, rather than something pervasive. Create test phrases of five to ten words that contain your brand names, technical terms, or foreign language phrases. Based on the outputs, decide whether you want to use a pronunciation dictionary or just phonetic tags for each. Speech models might occasionally adopt a strange or slow cadence mid-sentence. This often happens when the model has to guess how to pronounce a passage that differs from what it saw in training. When you know what to watch for, you’ll generate high-quality voice content faster and with fewer headaches. articles.title: How Fundación Televisa interviewed more than 1,000 entrepreneurs with voice AI
articles.description: Fundación Televisa used ElevenAgents to interview more than 1,000 entrepreneurs for POSiBLE, Mexico’s largest entrepreneurship accelerator.
articles.content: Introducing Eleven v4Meet Eleven v4, our most emotive model yet. Andrés Chama runs his own business, Comuni, a digital platform that connects neighbors and makes civic participation easier, so his free time rarely lines up with office hours. When he applied to POSiBLE, Mexico’s largest entrepreneurship accelerator run by Fundación Televisa, he didn’t have to wait for an opening on a staff member’s calendar. He talked through his business with an AI interviewer when it suited him and got feedback as soon as the call ended. This summer, Fundación Televisa used ElevenAgents to interview more than 1,000 entrepreneurs applying to POSiBLE’s 2026 cohort. The interviews ran from June 29 to July 24, and the POSiBLE team then drew on those conversations to choose 70 ventures for its National Camp, the accelerator’s final stage. Fundación Televisa is a Mexican nonprofit with more than 20 years of experience running large programs in education, entrepreneurship, and digital inclusion. Its work reaches millions of people across Mexico each year. POSiBLE supports businesses at the early, operating, and growth stages with training and mentoring, plus a place in a national community. Another one of its programs, Bécalos, is one of the country’s largest scholarship initiatives. Programs of this size depend on one-on-one conversations, and those take time. Every POSiBLE applicant needs an interview about growth, customers, and sales before the team can make a fair selection. With more than a thousand applicants, scheduling those calls alone is a major undertaking. Fundación Televisa’s technology team began testing ElevenLabs in March, after a demo at the foundation’s Mexico City offices. Led by Julio Alberto Ramos, the foundation’s CTO, the team connected ElevenLabs to its existing chat systems through the API. In June, the foundation joined the ElevenLabs Impact Program, which supports nonprofits with our voice AI tools. ElevenLabs’ Mexico team worked with Ramos and his colleagues on agent setup, call capacity, and integration with POSiBLE’s web platform. Interviews averaged five minutes. Applicants opened a voice agent embedded in POSiBLE’s web platform and talked through their business, from revenue to customer base. Because the agent was available any time of day, founders could interview whenever their schedules allowed. By the time the window closed, the agent had conducted 1,036 interviews. Lizbeth Salazar, Data and AI Strategy Lead at POSiBLE, said the voice agent was the main engine behind the entire interview stage. “At POSiBLE, we believe that behind every business there is a person, a story, and a dream," Salazar said. "Artificial intelligence allows us to reach more entrepreneurs, but more importantly, it gives us the opportunity to truly listen to them, understand their challenges, and recognize what they really need.” Applicants noticed how the conversations felt. “It had very natural language compared to other voice models,” said Karina Michel, an entrepreneur chosen to join the POSiBLE cohort. For Andrés Chama, flexibility mattered most. “I felt very comfortable, and in the end, the insights were quite accurate,” he said. “The feedback after the interview helped me a lot.” He added that the agent never replaced POSiBLE’s staff, but it let him move at his own pace. “Even though POSiBLE has an amazing team, having an AI available every day for every part of this process meant I could do it whenever I, as an entrepreneur, had the time,” he said. “That made it feel much more approachable.” The selected founders met in person at POSiBLE’s National Camp in Santa Fe, Mexico City, from September 30 to October 4. The camp focused on innovation, AI, and business strategy. During the event, Raúl Rodríguez, an account manager at ElevenLabs, and Pablo Rivas, a sales development representative, led a 90-minute workshop on using voice AI to automate and scale business processes. Many of the founders in the room had already used the technology once, as applicants. Attendees also learned about ElevenLabs Startup Grants, which help early-stage companies build with ElevenLabs. POSiBLE wasn’t the only Fundación Televisa program to use voice agents. Bécalos, the foundation’s scholarship program, used ElevenAgents to conduct interviews for Bécalos English Challenge Movilidad. With the agent available 24 hours a day on July 7 and 8, it interviewed 394 young people in two days. Fundación Televisa is gearing up for its next POSiBLE cohort. Nonprofits working to expand access to education, opportunity, and information can apply to the Impact Program. Gabi leads Impact at ElevenLabs, democratizing access to voice AI for the people who need it most. The Impact Program helps people with ALS and other conditions that can cause permanent voice loss preserve or reclaim their voices, while expanding access to audio AI tools for nonprofits, cultural institutions, and educators around the world. Before joining ElevenLabs, Gabi was a voice-specialized speech-language pathologist, using voice science and research to support patients with complex voice disorders. She received her Master's in Speech, Language, and Learning from Northwestern University and completed her clinical fellowship at the University of Miami. articles.title: ElevenAgents for Healthcare: Build an outbound appointment reminder agent with Architect
articles.description: Build an outbound voice agent on ElevenAgents that verifies patients and confirms, reschedules, or cancels appointments in the EHR during the call.
articles.content: Introducing Eleven v4Meet Eleven v4, our most emotive model yet. Nearly one in four healthcare appointments never happens. A systematic review of 105 studies put the average no-show rate at 23%, and in an August poll, 32% of medical groups said rates were higher in 2026 than in 2025, up from 27% a year earlier. Record deductibles are leading patients to second-guess visits they booked six weeks ago. The cost shows up in revenue, but also in a screening that slips or a follow-up that turns into an urgent visit. This post shows how to build an outbound voice agent on ElevenAgents that calls patients before a visit, verifies their date of birth, and confirms, reschedules, or cancels the appointment in the electronic health record (EHR) during the call. The slot goes back into inventory while there’s still time to fill it. The agent was built with Architect, the assistant inside ElevenAgents, and it can run as a nightly batch or in real time from EHR events. The approach is already working. Everlywell uses ElevenAgents to remind members about eligible screenings, and it saw a 10% improvement in screening completion versus traditional interactive voice response (IVR), with 3.5x higher conversion among Spanish-speaking members. Ovianta uses ElevenAgents to follow up after treatment proposals, reaching a 68% patient engagement rate, a 25% increase in treatment conversion, and an 83% reduction in manual follow-up calls for clinic staff. This is the second post in a healthcare series. The first covered an inbound scheduling agent that answers when patients call to book. To run the outbound agent across a whole patient list, care teams can use Campaign Manager, now in ElevenAgents. It handles calling windows, local-time dialing, retries, and voicemail, and it tracks every patient in one funnel from first call to confirmed visit. Most practices already run some kind of reminder program. Front-desk staff calling patients by hand is difficult to scale. These types of calls happen only during business hours, using the same people who answer the inbound line, so it stops once the schedule gets busy. Text and email reminders are inexpensive to run, able to reach everyone, but usually run one way. Engagement drops for older patients and for anyone whose first language isn't the one the text was written in. Automated IVR calls sit in between these methods. They scale, and they use the phone. However, a “press-1-to-confirm” menu still cannot handle a reschedule, cannot verify identity to any real standard, and hands off badly when the patient asks a question. Outsourced call centers give you human conversations at volume, but at a high cost-per-call. This approach comes with quality that varies by shift and with more people handling protected health information outside your organization. The research points one way on delivery: a reminder that reaches the patient live does far better than one that doesn't. A Veterans Health Administration study found a 3% no-show rate when a phone reminder reached the patient live, 24% when it went to voicemail, and 39% when nobody answered and no voicemail was left. For many health systems, only a front-desk call can verify the patient and change the schedule in the same touch, but it doesn't scale. With ElevenAgents, health systems can now proactively reach patients, make real-time changes to their schedule, and scale their outreach. The outbound reminder agent runs on the same platform, tools, and security review as the inbound scheduling agent, so one vendor covers both the front door and the follow-up. It calls the patient ahead of the visit, confirms their identity, and reads the live appointment from the EHR. From there, it confirms, reschedules, or cancels the appointment against the provider’s open slots. The agent also handles the edge cases. If the call goes to voicemail, it leaves a message. If a patient asks not to be called again, it records the opt-out so no future calls go out. If a patient wants to talk to a person, it transfers to the front desk. A nightly export can trigger it as a scheduled batch, or real-time EHR events can trigger it one call at a time. ElevenLabs built this agent with Architect, the assistant inside ElevenAgents that reads and edits an agent’s configuration, workflow, tools, and tests from a chat. The previous post configured every node by hand. This time, the call was described in plain language, and Architect built the workflow. To build the outbound agent, you’ll need: Seed one synthetic patient and one appointment so the agent has something to remind you about: Then seed a Schedule for the provider and a handful of free Slots on it: one POST /Schedule, and one POST /Slot per opening with a schedule reference, status free, and a UTC start and end. Keep the three IDs. The patient ID becomes patient_id (and, prefixed with Patient/, patient_reference), the appointment ID becomes appointment_id, and the schedule becomes fhir_schedule_id. The agent is the same no matter how a call starts. What differs is the trigger, which determines freshness, cost and compliance posture. Let’s imagine that each evening, a job queries the EHR for tomorrow's appointments: The job flattens each appointment into one row and converts the UTC timestamp into clinic-local words, because the agent reads the time aloud and a TTS model should not be guessing how. phone_number is the only required column. Every other column becomes a dynamic variable the agent can use in its prompt, first message and tool calls: Phone_number, patient_first_name, patient_last_name, patient_id, patient_reference, appointment_id, appointment_date, appointment_time, provider_name, visit_type, clinic_name, clinic_callback_number , +15550100199, Maria, Okonkwo, 81660, Patient/81660,81661,"Tuesday, October sixth", ten a.m., Dr. Okafor, follow-up visit, Lakeside Family Medicine, "five five five, zero one zero zero", +15550100244, Daniel, Reyes, 81702, Patient/81702, 81718, "Tuesday, October sixth", nine thirty a.m., Dr. Okafor, annual physical, Lakeside Family Medicine, "five five five, zero one zero zero" That file goes to Batch Calling, uploaded in the dashboard or submitted through the API. You pick the agent, the outbound number and a start time inside your calling window. Batch calls draw on a capped share of concurrency (the lower of 50% of the workspace limit or 70% of the agent's), so a big reminder run doesn't starve the inbound line. The export job also owns the retry policy. Anyone who ended in voicemail or no answer goes back on the next day's list at a different hour. Three attempts per patient per week is the ceiling, and a confirmed, canceled, rescheduled or opted-out outcome removes them. The export job owns every retry decision. For a practice that books most visits more than a day out, batch is the right default and the least work. Batch has a blind spot: anything that changes after the export, such as same-day bookings, a patient who moved from 8am to 3pm, or a slot that opened after a cancellation. For those, a small trigger service listens to appointment events from the EHR (a FHIR Subscription, a webhook from the practice management system, or a job that polls every few minutes) and places one call at a time through the outbound call API: twilio_machine_detection turns on Twilio-side answering machine detection alongside the agent's own voicemail tool, which we cover under Tools. And because each call starts individually, it can run under Zero Retention Mode, which batch calls cannot. Same-day changes; deployments that require ZRM A practical setup runs both. Batch carries the bulk of next-day reminders, while the real-time path picks up whatever moved after the export and anything that must run under ZRM. The agent reads the appointment from FHIR and changes it in FHIR. Open times come from Slot, a reschedule is a PUT on the same Appointment the agent just confirmed, and a cancel sets its status. There is nothing to reconcile against the chart afterward, the EHR is correct the moment the call ends, and every write the agent makes is a FHIR resource your audit log already covers. The post-call webhook still carries the outcome to anything downstream. If your practice runs a separate scheduling system, swap the three scheduling tools for that system's API; the two workflow nodes stay the same. Patient outreach is difficult if the phone shows "Spam Likely." Before the first batch, register the outbound number so calls carry full STIR/SHAKEN attestation, set CNAM so the clinic name displays, and look at Twilio's branded calling options for the carriers your patients are on, because a reminder that gets screened doesn’t happen. In the inbound post, every node, tool and edge condition was configured by hand. Here we started with an agent that had the FHIR tools attached, the system tools enabled, a base prompt covering role, boundaries and how to speak, and nine simulation tests. No workflow. We opened the Architect tab and described the call: Build an outbound appointment reminder workflow for this agent. Open by stating the clinic name, that this is an automated call about an upcoming appointment, and asking for the patient by first name using the patient_first_name dynamic variable. If the person who answers is not the patient, do not share any appointment details, offer a callback window, and end the call. Once we are speaking to the patient, ask for their date of birth and verify it with @fhir_get_patient. Treat total 1 as verified. Allow one retry on a mismatch, then end the call. After verification, call @fhir_get_appointment and confirm the appointment using what it returns. If the patient confirms, recap and close. If they want to reschedule, ask what day suits them, call @fhir_get_available_slots for that day, offer at most two of the returned slots in clinic time, and when they choose call @fhir_reschedule_appointment with that slot's exact start, end and id. Say the new time is booked only after that call succeeds. If they want to cancel, confirm once, call @fhir_cancel_appointment, and offer to rebook from the same slots. If a scheduling tool fails twice, do not transfer; say the original appointment still stands and the office will call back. If they ask for a person twice or describe urgent symptoms, tell them you are connecting them and transfer to the front desk. Route every transfer through a short notice node so the patient always hears that line first. Architect built the workflow in stages, pausing twice: once to ask about unsaved edits in the editor, and once to ask whether to finish the rest of the flow before publishing. Architect came back with eleven nodes and named them itself: a start node, Confirm who answered, Not the patient: offer callback, Verify date of birth, Confirm appointment, Reschedule, Cancel, Recap and close, a Transfer notice node that speaks one fixed line, a Front desk transfer node, and an end node. Tool scoping landed correctly. fhir_get_patient lives only on Verify. fhir_get_appointment lives only on Confirm. The scheduling tools live on Reschedule and Cancel. Architect also removed the agent-level transfer_to_number tool so the only path to the front desk runs through the notice node, and it flagged two things it could not finish on its own: a setting on the Transfer notice node that had not saved, and two lines in our base prompt that still told the agent to call a tool that no longer existed. Architect offered to rewrite those lines or run the tests, and we had it rewrite both. Five of nine passed. Two of the failures were exactly what a reminder agent exists to prevent. In the confirm scenario, the agent read out "Monday, October fifth at two p.m. with Dr. Okafor," the moment the patient said "yeah, this is Jack," before any date of birth had been checked and identity verified. articles.content: Codyone Cameron, a 32-year-old Wisconsin resident, holds the ultrasound from her visit to a crisis pregnancy center called Life’s Connection. A doctor at another clinic she visited later told Cameron that the ultrasound was not of her uterus, but her intestines, and the area marked as a baby was likely stool. (Photo courtesy of Center for Reproductive Rights)A Wisconsin woman is asking the state attorney general’s office to investigate anti-abortion crisis pregnancy centers after she says one of them failed to diagnose an ectopic pregnancy that caused her to need emergency surgery and resulted in the loss of her fertility. Codyone Cameron, a 32-year-old Milwaukee resident, worked with the progressive legal advocacy group Center for Reproductive Rights to send a letter to Wisconsin Attorney General Josh Kaul, a Democrat, asking for a formal investigation into whether pregnancy centers are engaging in deceptive trade and fundraising practices and the unlicensed practice of medicine. Riley Vetterkind, a spokesperson for Kaul, said the office does not confirm or deny the existence of investigations except in rare cases of public safety. Crisis pregnancy centers are organizations that typically advertise free pregnancy tests and ultrasounds, with an overarching goal of preventing and dissuading women from seeking an abortion. Many of them are affiliated with national anti-abortion organizations, including Heartbeat International, Care Net, and National Institute of Family and Life Advocates, and receiving funding from other national religious groups. States Newsroom published an investigative series earlier this year showing that 21 states directed more than $491 million in state funds to crisis pregnancy centers between fiscal years 2022 and 2025, with little oversight or accountability for how it is spent. Wisconsin lawmakers enacted a bill in 2025 appropriating $69,100 in fiscal years 2026 and 2027 for grants for pregnancy counseling programs, which was listed by the Lozier Institute as a program for crisis pregnancy centers. Lozier is a division of Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America, a national anti-abortion organization that partners with one of the largest crisis pregnancy center networks, Care Net. It’s unclear whether those dollars have been sent to the anti-abortion centers this fiscal year. Crisis pregnancy centers have also been promoted by the federal government. Earlier this year, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services launched a website called moms.gov that directs people to the anti-abortion centers in their area, as well as to federally qualified health centers. The center that Cameron visited, Life’s Connection, is listed on that website. The centers exist in an unregulated gray area by advertising “limited” ultrasounds, and some clinics make sure to say those ultrasounds are non-diagnostic. Life’s Connection’s website says, “Schedule an ultrasound to be sure you have a viable pregnancy.” When reached by phone on Thursday, a staff member at Life’s Connection told Stateline they do not speak to the media and did not want to respond to any of the allegations made by Cameron. Continued pain, then surgery Cameron had a history of ectopic pregnancy, said Alice Wang, senior staff attorney for the Center for Reproductive Rights, a legal advocacy organization based in Washington, D.C. Cameron has two children, and her third pregnancy was ectopic, which occurs when an embryo implants in a location other than the uterus, most often in the fallopian tube. Such pregnancies are never viable and can become life-threatening if untreated. Because of that history, Cameron said, she felt the same type of pain in August after learning she was pregnant and was concerned it was also ectopic. She called an OB-GYN clinic but couldn’t get an appointment for a few weeks, Wang said, and wanted to be seen sooner. A health provider listed in a directory under the state’s Medicaid program told Cameron to call Life’s Connection, where she got an appointment. Quotation The provider told her, I’m so sorry, these are not photos of your uterus. – Alice Wang, senior staff attorney for the Center for Reproductive Rights In the letter to the attorney general, Cameron said she told a Life’s Connection worker dressed in medical scrubs that she was concerned her pregnancy was ectopic. The staffer, the letter said, performed an ultrasound and reassured her that the baby was inside her uterus, identifying a “yolk sac” and providing measurements with a due date. Feeling reassured, Cameron disregarded the symptoms, and more than a week later, the pain had increased to a point she could no longer ignore it, according to the letter. She went to a community clinic that provides comprehensive reproductive healthcare, Care for All, where a doctor said the picture of her ultrasound appeared to be part of Cameron’s intestines, and that the staffer at the crisis pregnancy center had identified stool inside of her intestines as a baby. “The provider told her, I’m so sorry, these are not photos of your uterus,” Wang said. After further testing, the doctor at Care for All told her the pregnancy was likely ectopic and she needed to go straight to the emergency room. There, she was told she needed immediate surgery to remove both of the fallopian tubes because of the ectopic pregnancy’s advanced stage and further risks. “Ms. Cameron can no longer achieve pregnancy without the aid of in vitro fertilization — an expensive procedure that has no guarantee of success, is not covered by Medicaid, and which she cannot afford to pay out of pocket,” the letter said. Quick appointments, free services draw people in Cameron’s case is not the first ectopic pregnancy missed by a crisis pregnancy center. A woman in Texas reported a similar experience in 2025 with a center that assured her the pregnancy was in the right place and normal, according to news reports, and a Massachusetts woman sued a clinic in 2022 for misleading her about her ectopic pregnancy, which ruptured and caused serious internal bleeding, requiring emergency surgery. Taxpayer dollars flood pregnancy centers. Oversight hasn’t followed. Dr. Anwar Jackson, a Milwaukee-based OB-GYN, said he often sees patients who went to a crisis pregnancy center before coming to see him. Wisconsin, like many other states nationwide, has a shortage of OB-GYN providers, and he said at his particular clinic, it can take up to two months to get an appointment, even for a pregnant patient. The quick availability of appointments at the crisis pregnancy centers plus the promise of free care is what draws people in, he said. “A lot of times people will try to figure out where they can go for cheap, and CPCs take advantage of that by offering free services,” Jackson said. “In the end, it doesn’t change much, because they still have to go back into the healthcare system, a lot of times through the emergency room, which can be even more expensive.” Jackson said someone with basic levels of ultrasound training should know whether they are looking at the intestines or a uterus. Dr. Kristin Lyerly, a Wisconsin-based OB-GYN, said she had a similar story of a patient who had the wrong part of her body scanned. When she worked at Planned Parenthood, Lyerly said a patient came in who had been to a pregnancy center and had a copy of an ultrasound of her bladder rather than her uterus. Lyerly is also heavily involved in legislative advocacy work, and noted the legislature will have Democratic majorities in the House and Senate next year, with women leadership, and a Democratic governor who is supportive of reproductive health issues. She and others plan to push for legislative action to regulate crisis pregnancy centers in Wisconsin in the upcoming session, which is scheduled to begin in early January. “I’m hoping that we will have a robust agenda coming out of the gate,” Lyerly said. articles.content: A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement vehicle is parked outside a Roxbury, N.J., warehouse slated to become a migrant detention center. The nonpartisan Government Accountability Office urged federal immigration authorities to plan immigration detention more carefully to avoid more wasted taxpayer funds, in a new report. (Photo by Benjamin Leynse/New Jersey Monitor)The nonpartisan Government Accountability Office urged federal immigration authorities to plan immigration detention costs more carefully to avoid more wasted taxpayer funds, in a new report released Thursday. Immigration and Customs Enforcement budgeted $2.8 billion for detention in the 2025 fiscal year, more than 40% above the previous year, but then scaled back an unpopular move to buy 11 warehouses and convert them to hold detainees. That pullback resulted in millions of dollars in waste, according to a previous GAO report, and ICE has yet to make a new plan for the money, the new GAO report stated. Millions of dollars of waste found in Trump administration push for immigration detention Costs per prisoner range from $85 a day for state and local jails to $180 a day for federal prisons, and ICE needs to make a new plan to “reduce potential waste and help ensure the cost effective use of taxpayer dollars,” the report states. Not all the warehouse conversion plans will be reversed. As recently as Nov. 5, ICE informed New Jersey that it still plans to convert a Roxbury warehouse into an immigration detention center after environmental review. Another proposal in Arizona is open for public comment until Dec. 9. ICE, however, has announced plans to sell other warehouses in Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Texas and Utah. There have also been purchases of private prisons — such as one in Minnesota that drew fire for its high price compared with an earlier offer, and a deal announced this week to buy a private prison in Washington state.
